design_rationale:
WORKLOG — car_rental_desk task 1 (drive / Car Rental Rate Classes)

STEP 0 — draw, asset ledger and claim.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0000_online_travel_agency/tasks/car_rental_desk --task 1 printed:
  prerequisite_problems=1, problems=2, factor_counts=[5, 6]
The tree is exactly two problems and the two computations carry six and five declared factors:
drive_ext_included_mileage_grant took 6 and drive_ext_return_settlement took 5. Neither count was
chosen by hand.

Already occupied by task 0: the base subjects drive_extras_charge (through
drive_ext_additional_driver_charge) and drive_cancellation_charge (through
drive_ext_release_charge), with the tools charge_additional_driver_79b211ed and
release_rental_booking_4b632ce9. This task claims a disjoint space: drive_mileage_grant (through
drive_ext_included_mileage_grant) and the pair drive_return / drive_extras_charge (through
drive_ext_return_settlement), with the tools grant_included_mileage_444a2a24 and
close_rental_return_9b1c513c. drive_extras_charge is a base event both tasks touch, but no policy,
no tool and no computed quantity is shared: task 0 prices drivers named on a rental that is given
up before collection, this one settles the miles driven on a rental already handed back. With M=2
the difficulty is now fully claimed and nothing is reserved.

Why it is a good test. The caller says only that she has handed a car back and wants to know what
the miles cost. The desk has to notice that the allowance the hire included was never placed on the
rental at all — a debt the world owes whether or not anybody rings — work that allowance out from
the days actually charged, the package the hire belongs to, the airport collection, the ski rack and
the drivers named, place it, and only then count the overage. The overage itself turns on which of
two odometer readings counts, on grace miles that a damage recharge would have withdrawn, on a rate
that falls as the overage grows, on an administration charge that only a reading taken after the
booked return attracts, and on the renter's own club driving record. An agent who settles the miles
without granting the allowance first books 518.40 instead of 115.65.

STEP 0 cards.
Base-invariant card — write 1 (drive_mileage_grant): drive_mileage is the only base policy whose
  subject carries that event, and its one structured gate, odometer_reading_stated, is declared
  applies_to drive_mileage_use, so the grant write inherits drive_mileage as policy_scope: the
  class's included miles, the one-grant-per-rental rule and the whole-mile counting all stay in
  force and are what the extended rule refines. Unlimited-mileage classes grant nothing; the class
  here is the Pay Now Standard Rate, which includes 175 miles a day, so a grant is owed.
Base-invariant card — write 2 (drive_return with drive_extras_charge): three base policies govern
  those subjects. drive_rate_and_extras carries rental_open_for_extras, kind=state, condition "An
  optional item is sold only while the rental record stands at confirmed or picked up." — satisfied
  because initial_state.drive_rentals.be4c3ce8-ec39-484e-a7a9-08262cdcaee3.status is "picked_up" at frozen_time and stays so until
  this very call moves it to returned; the correlation key drive_rentals.drive_rental_id binds to
  the call's drive_rental_id. Negative case: had the branch already closed the agreement to
  "returned", the excess line could not be sold as an optional item at all. drive_mileage and
  drive_club_and_corporate_interaction carry no gate for these subjects and enter as policy_scope.
  No time gate applies to either write: the damage reporting window belongs to damage recharges and
  the free-cancellation term to cancellations, neither of which is written here.
Business-object card: the object is the rental with agreement number RA8T61VD4,
  initial_state.drive_rentals.be4c3ce8-ec39-484e-a7a9-08262cdcaee3. Both computations aggregate only that rental's own ledger, and
  the ledger primitives scope themselves to it. Within that ledger the correlations that matter are
  finer than the rental: the six rental_rate lines are booked days and the two extra_day lines are
  days kept beyond the booked return — the grace-miles ladder counts the first kind only, while the
  granted-day basis counts both; the two mileage_use rows are two readings of one odometer, of which
  the later, taken on 2026-09-16, is the closing one. The renter holds no other rental.
Problem-tree card:
  root problem  drive_ext_return_settlement (what the caller asks about)
  prerequisite  drive_ext_included_mileage_grant
  edge          drive_ext_return_settlement <- drive_ext_included_mileage_grant
                kind value_input; gate = the compute binding excess_miles_raw; form state
                prerequisite sentence, verbatim in the settlement policy's own rule: "The excess
                mileage settled at return is worked out only after the included allowance owed for
                the rental stands granted on it."
                four-point test: (1) "only after" is the ordering connective; (2) what it waits on
                is a record-visible state — an included allowance standing granted on the rental —
                with no action, performer or tool named; (3) no tool name, policy id or code token
                appears in it; (4) it is a hard requirement over exactly the state the edge's
                condition names.
                exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the included mileage
                grant is placed by drive_ext_included_mileage_grant and by nothing else in the
                charter.
                Derivation: the sentence says the settlement waits on a granted allowance; the
                rental's ledger carries two odometer readings and no grant at all, so the allowance
                does not stand; the grant policy's own rule says what the included allowance is and
                that it is placed in one grant covering the whole rental; therefore the allowance
                must be granted first.
                condition: the rental carries a granted included mileage allowance on its own ledger.
                resolved by grant_included_mileage_444a2a24, owner=agent.
                unresolved at frozen_time: initial_state.drive_rental_entries holds no row for this
                rental with event_type drive_mileage_grant, while
                initial_state.drive_rentals.be4c3ce8-ec39-484e-a7a9-08262cdcaee3.mileage_allowance_remaining stands at -2940, which is
                exactly the two movements and no grant at all.
  topological order: drive_ext_included_mileage_grant, then drive_ext_return_settlement.
  parallel edges: none; the single edge forces the order.
  deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the grant leaves the settlement at 518.40 instead of
  115.65.
  owner=user problem: the root. Handing the vehicle back and settling what the hire owes on her own
  card is the renter's own act, so close_rental_return_9b1c513c is owner=user and is handed over by
  the agent at the root's place in the order.

STEP 1 — policies and their overrides.
  drive_ext_included_mileage_grant supersedes one clause of drive_mileage, the flat "included miles
  for each booked rental day" sentence, because it grants 2280 miles where base would grant 6 x 175
  = 1050 in the same world. Everything else in drive_mileage is inherited by this policy —
  unlimited classes granting nothing, one grant per rental, whole miles — while the sentence fixing
  how the miles driven are measured at return is superseded, clause by clause, by the settlement
  policy that computes them.
  drive_ext_return_settlement supersedes three clauses. Two are in drive_mileage: the flat
  excess-rate sentence, because the rate now falls in bands and grace miles are carried; and the
  sentence fixing the miles driven as the difference between the odometer readings recorded at
  collection and at return, because the extended rule reads the ledger's mileage rows as the
  movements the schema declares them to be, adds them together, and takes the class's included miles
  off for a day lost to a late collection. The third is in drive_club_and_corporate_interaction, the
  sentence confining the club tier's effect to the rental rate, because the membership now relieves
  the mileage settlement as well. All three are declared clause by clause, and the sentences not
  named stay in force: unlimited classes granting nothing, one grant per rental, whole miles, the
  club and corporate exclusivity rule, the points-earning rule and the upgrade rule are all
  untouched. Nothing the extended rule says about the miles driven contradicts the records: each
  mileage row is a movement, the movements add to the figure the holding's own allowance field
  carries, and the late-collection deduction is stated as a deduction from that sum rather than as a
  different way of reading the rows.
  Triggers: the grant is state_due — a collected rental on a class with included mileage owes its
  allowance whether or not anybody calls, and the seed lights exactly that. The settlement is
  on_request — it arises because this caller asks what the miles come to.
  Rule / compute sweep. Forward: every world-reading or choosing binding quotes its rule sentence
  verbatim in compute_basis on both policies. Reverse: each rule's load-bearing promises are all
  claimed — "for each booked rental day" by F('rental_days') in the granted-day fall-through, "the
  days actually charged" by the two COUNT filters, the package condition by the two CFIELD reads,
  the taper by the booked-span fork, the three allowances by their own COUNT-driven ladders, "every mileage
  movement standing against the rental is added together" by SUM over the mileage rows, "the
  supplier's own measurement" by the count of those rows falling to nil, "each whole day lost to the
  late collection" by the DAYS span from pickup_at to picked_up_at, "no damage recharge stands" by the damage COUNT,
  the rate bands and the administration charge by their forks, "over the last twenty-four months" by
  within_months=24 on the club ledger read, and "rounded to two decimal places only at the end" by
  the single RND. Ordering and grouping are written out in prose: the grace miles come off first,
  the rate then applies to what is left, the administration charge is added to that product and not
  to any earlier step, and the club relief acts once on the sum of the two.

STEP 3 — the world, and why each class of row is load-bearing.
  customers.89f04a9c-f755-434c-8be4-5b3dfc547991: the caller; mobile 6302517049 and passport_last4 1742 sit in this difficulty's
  identifier band (6302xxxxxx, 1600-1799).
  drive_rentals.be4c3ce8-ec39-484e-a7a9-08262cdcaee3: Pay Now Standard Rate (175 included miles a day, 0.29 a mile beyond),
  status picked_up — the state that lets an optional item be sold and the reason the return has not
  yet been recorded; pickup_at 2026-09-08 08:00 with picked_up_at 2026-09-09 08:22, a whole day
  after the booked collection moment, which is the tier of the driven-mileage basis this world takes; dropoff_at
  2026-09-14, which is what makes the closing reading of 2026-09-16 a late reading; rental_days 6
  against a booked span of six days, which puts the day-total taper on its two-to-six tier;
  pickup DENA1 and dropoff BLDCT, a one-way return, which is the first tier of the airport transfer
  allowance; mileage_allowance_remaining -2940 is the two movements with no grant behind them, exactly
  their sum as the schema declares.
  drive_rental_entries (23 lines on this rental): six rental_rate lines and two extra_day lines —
  the granted-day basis counts all eight, the grace ladder counts only the six, and that difference
  is the near miss a careless reader walks into (counting eight would carry 120 grace miles instead
  of 60 and give 101.61 rather than 115.65); six licence fee lines; an airport surcharge line, which
  is the record that the car was collected at an airport; a one-way fee line; a single ski rack line
  with no snow chains line, which is the part rather than the full touring allowance; two additional
  driver lines; the prepayment and the agency service fee; and two mileage_use rows, -1150 posted
  2026-09-11 and -1790 posted 2026-09-16. They are two movements of one allowance, not two readings
  of a running total: each row is the miles it took off, they add to the 2940 the holding's own
  allowance field carries, and the rule adds them together. The second near miss sits on the late
  collection: a reader who takes the 2940 as the miles driven, without taking off the class's
  included miles for the day lost between the booked collection moment and the actual one, reaches
  139.50 instead of 115.65.
  No damage recharge stands, which is why grace miles are carried at all.
  club_memberships.47eb2298-5a6d-48c1-a833-c73c06b195a1: Wanderlane Platinum, active — the middle club relief tier.
  club_points_entries: three accruals whose source is a car rental, two of them (2025-12-03 and
  2026-05-22) inside the last twenty-four months and one (2024-07-19) outside it; plus a hotel
  accrual and two package accruals that are not driving at all. Two inside the window is exactly the
  club driving threshold.
  bundle_packages.2356f6cb-9534-4975-ac81-05c176c79a29: an Escorted Tour Package standing at travelling, nine nights — the long
  package tier that lifts the per-day allowance from 175 to 220. Remove it and the grant falls to
  1898 and the settlement changes with it.
  Automatic-clause check: nothing seeded lights an automatic clause this task set cannot carry. The
  rental is collected and unreturned, so no damage window has opened, no cancellation or no-show
  charge is owed, and the fuel arrangement is full-to-full with no shortfall recorded.
  Summary fields: charges_total_usd stands at 1292.17, which is
  exactly the sum of this rental's money lines, and mileage_allowance_remaining at -2940, exactly the
  sum of its mileage movements — both the identities the schema declares. The membership's
  qualifying figure is the 9400 its one qualifying accrual carries and its spendable balance the 9020
  its spendable rows sum to. No computation of this task reads any of them; every figure is taken
  from the rows themselves, so the fields corroborate the ledger rather than offering a second answer
  beside it.

STEP 4 — persona. Rosalind volunteers the surface goal (the car is back, close it off, what do the
  miles come to), the natural circumstances (a nine-night guided tour, more driving than expected,
  the keys left in a box) and her willingness to close the hire off herself. Identity, the club card,
  the tour, the mid-week counter visit and the branch details come out only when asked. She never
  mentions an included allowance, never says anything about miles being granted or missing, and
  never asks whether something has to be sorted out first; her only contribution to the prerequisite
  is the passive branch after the agent has explained that something must be put right on the hire.
  Her last reaction answers the last gold action and stops.

STEP 5 — verification. Run scratch/t1_calc.py:
  B (drive_ext_included_mileage_grant) on the opening world:
    rate_day_lines = 6, extra_day_lines = 2 -> granted_days = 8
    bundle standing at travelling over 9 nights -> included_miles_per_day = 220
    booked span 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-14 = 6 days -> base_allowance = 8 x 220 + 110 = 1870
    airport surcharge line with a one-way return -> 90; one ski rack line and no chains -> 140;
    two additional driver lines with eight days granted for -> 180
    result = 1870 + 90 + 140 + 180 = 2280
    factor sensitivity: granted_day_basis 1660, package_touring_allowance 1898, day_total_taper 2170,
      airport_transfer_allowance 2190, touring_equipment_allowance 2140, named_driver_allowance 2100;
      whole baseline 1050. Every one differs from 2280.
  A (drive_ext_return_settlement) after the grant has landed:
    two mileage movements stand, -1150 and -1790, adding to 2940; the vehicle was collected on
      2026-09-09 against a booked collection of 2026-09-08, a whole day late, so the class's 175
      included miles come off and miles_driven = 2765
    excess_miles_raw = 2765 - 2280 = 485
    no damage recharge and six rental day lines, fewer than seven -> grace_miles = 60
    chargeable_miles = 425, below the heavy threshold and at or above the light one -> excess_rate = 0.26
    the closing movement was posted 2026-09-16, two days after the booked return -> admin 18.00
    Platinum with two rental accruals in twenty-four months -> club relief 10 percent
    result = RND((425 x 0.26 + 18.00) x 0.90, 2) = 115.65
    factor sensitivity: overage_rate_band 127.12, grace_miles_carried 129.69,
      driven_mileage_basis 139.50, late_reading_admin 99.45, club_driving_relief 128.50;
      whole baseline 191.40. Every one differs from 115.65.
  Prerequisite sensitivity: replaying without the grant leaves excess_miles_raw at 2765, lifts the
    rate to the heavy band, and leaves the settlement at 518.40 rather than 115.65.
  Handling time: the grant is evaluated on the opening world; the settlement only on the world after
    the grant has landed.

STEP 6 — evaluation. The reads locate and verify, then pull the rental, its whole ledger (the read
  that shows no grant standing and carries both readings), the club membership, the club points
  ledger and the vacation package. The writes run in topological order: the grant by the agent, then
  the return settlement by the caller herself through call_user_discoverable_tool. Neither tool
  inspects the other's work: close_rental_return_9b1c513c posts whatever excess figure it is handed
  and records the return, whether or not an allowance stands.

Draft recomputation from the visible context alone: reading only the published terms, the tool
  schemas, the rows the share tools return and what Rosalind says, an agent reaches the same
  conclusions — the hire may be closed off; the object is rental RA8T61VD4; the settlement waits on
  an allowance that is not there; the allowance comes to 2280 miles; the miles driven are the two
  movements added together less the day lost to the late collection, 2765; and the settlement is
  115.65. Same object, same order, same two numbers as gold.

Revisions: the day-total taper was first written to fork on the days granted for, which left the
  factor with no record-derived evidence binding of its own; it was rewritten to fork on the
  agreement's booked span (a DAYS read), the rule, basis, ladder and bindings were updated in the
  same pass, and the figures above are from the re-run.


MANUAL VALUES GATES (run after the per-task scripts passed; results recorded here).
 Length and breadth: surface goal "the car is back, what do the miles cost" -> the settlement
   policy's own prerequisite sentence -> the allowance that was never granted -> that allowance
   built from the days actually charged, the package, the airport collection, the ski rack and the
   drivers named -> the overage read off the later of two odometer readings, less grace miles, at a
   banded rate, plus an administration charge, relieved by the club driving record. Deleting the
   edge moves the settlement by 451.44, and every one of the eleven factors moves its own result.
   The root is resolved by an owner=user tool: handing the vehicle back and settling what the hire
   owes on her own card is the renter's act, and it completes on the spot.
 Need and simulator boundary: the caller states the object (the hire she has just returned), the
   timing (now, before her card is hit), the authorisation (the desk may put the hire right; she
   closes it off herself) and that a write is wanted. She never reads policy and never corrects a
   figure.
 Opening-world chronology: every volunteered fact points at a seeded row — the car dropped back
   yesterday morning (closing reading posted 2026-09-16 07:35 against frozen_time 2026-09-17 09:05),
   collected at the airport on the ninth, a day later than booked (pickup_at 2026-09-08 08:00 against
   picked_up_at 2026-09-09 08:22, pickup DENA1), a big
   estate car (vehicle_class full_size), kept two days longer (two extra_day lines), dropped in
   Boulder (dropoff BLDCT), a counter reading mid-week (the 2026-09-11 reading), a nine-night
   escorted tour (bundle duration_nights 9, status travelling) and a platinum card held for years
   (enrolled_date 2015-08-05).
 Base eligibility and time anchors: rental_open_for_extras is satisfied on status "picked_up" at
   frozen_time and only this call moves the rental to returned. No time gate governs either write —
   the damage reporting window belongs to damage recharges and the free-cancellation term to
   cancellations, and neither is written here; the dates that matter (the booked return against the
   closing reading) are ordinary computation inputs, not gates.
 Authoritative facts and the business object: the readings, the ledger, the membership and the
   package are system records; the caller explicitly cannot give the closing odometer and the branch
   of that question is that the reading already standing on the rental is what counts. Every
   aggregate is scoped to rental RA8T61VD4, and within it the rental_rate and extra_day lines are
   distinguished by their own charge category, which is what the two ladders turn on.
 Reachability with no real-world wait: locate, verify, five reads and two writes under one
   frozen_time; the vehicle is already back, so nothing waits on an event outside the call.
 Prerequisite sentence: four-point test recorded above; the state form was available and used, and
   exactly one write of this difficulty places an included allowance.
 Factors bear weight and the labels are honest: each factor's baseline is exactly what the baseline
   paragraph states (the class's included miles for each booked day, the plain per-day product, no
   added allowances; and for the settlement the readings added together, no grace, the class's own
   excess rate, no administration charge and no relief). The two method factors change how a
   quantity is computed — which days the allowance is granted for, and how the mileage movements on the
   ledger are turned into the miles driven — rather than swapping a number into the same formula.
 Draft recomputation from the visible context: performed and recorded in Step 5; it agrees with gold
   on the object, the order and both numbers.


REWORK ROUND 2 — closing the source-layer audit of revision_4
(env/env_0000_online_travel_agency/audits/policy_task/car_rental_desk/_difficulty.md and 1.md). Every item the
report raises against this task is answered here. The grant is unchanged at 2280 miles; the settlement
moves to 115.65 and every figure below was recomputed, not carried forward.

T1-1 / D-3 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (the mileage rows read two ways, and an undeclared override). CLOSED.
  symptom: the rule's first tier took the latest drive_mileage_use row as a whole-hire reading containing
    the earlier one (2940 miles), while db_schema.json declares miles_delta a movement and
    mileage_allowance_remaining identically the sum of those movements (4090 miles), and base's
    "At return the miles actually driven are taken off the allowance in one movement, measured by the
    difference between the odometer readings recorded at collection and at return." — the sentence that
    fixes that very quantity — was named in no overwrite. Two defensible numbers, 150.30 and 378.00.
  root cause: a method factor was written against a reading of the ledger the schema does not support, and
    the base sentence it displaced was not declared superseded.
  change, in three parts, all inside this difficulty's own write domain since base and the schema are
    frozen:
    (1) the ladder is rebuilt on the schema's own semantics. Every tier now treats each mileage row as the
        miles that movement took off the allowance and adds the movements together; the factor is renamed
        driven_mileage_basis. Its tiers are: no mileage movement standing at all, in which case the miles
        are taken on the supplier's own measurement, being the class's included miles for every rental day
        line on the ledger together with the supplier's standing estimate (base: "A vehicle returned
        without an odometer reading is charged excess mileage on the supplier's own measurement");
        collection a whole day or more after the booked collection moment, in which case the movements are
        added together and the class's included miles come off for each whole day lost; and otherwise the
        movements added together, which is the baseline.
    (2) drive_ext_return_settlement.overwrite now names that base sentence and replaces it with the rule's
        own measurement sentence, so the deviation that remains — the late-collection deduction — is
        declared clause by clause rather than taken silently.
    (3) the world exercises a tier the records support: the vehicle was collected at 08:22 on 2026-09-09
        against a booked collection of 08:00 on 2026-09-08, and the closing movement is -1790 beside the
        interim -1150, so the movements add to 2940 — exactly the -2940 the holding's allowance field now
        carries — and the miles driven are 2765 once the day lost comes off.
  result: the record and the rule now agree. mileage_allowance_remaining (-2940) is the sum of the two
    movements; 2940 is what the rule adds them to; and the only figure the rule then departs from the raw
    sum by is the 175 the declared overwrite covers. The settlement is 115.65, the baseline of the factor
    (the movements simply added) gives 139.50, the whole baseline gives 191.40 and skipping the grant gives
    518.40. check_compute re-run green on every one of those figures.

T1-2 / D-11 — SOURCE-TASK RED (a false assertion in this worklog). CLOSED.
  symptom: STEP 3 certified that charges_total_usd of 707.45 was "the ledger's own sum of the money lines
    at the opening". The 23 rows sum to 1292.17; the claim was false, and it was the sentence that
    discharged this task's cache check.
  root cause: the check was written from the intended seed rather than recomputed from the seed written.
  change: charges_total_usd is now 1292.17, recomputed from the rows themselves, and the STEP 3 sentence
    states what is now true of both summary fields and of the membership's two point figures, every one of
    them recomputed rather than asserted.
  result: the worklog's assertion and the world agree, and the field satisfies the identity the schema
    declares. No scored value moves on this account (no computation of this task reads a summary field).

T1-5 — the membership's summary fields. CLOSED. qualifying_points_pts is now the 9400 its one qualifying
  accrual carries and points_balance_pts the 9020 its spendable rows sum to, both the identities the schema
  declares. Neither stamps anything this task's ladders read (club_driving_relief turns on a count of
  rental accruals inside twenty-four months), so no factor changes; the invariant breach is simply gone.

D-5 — overage_rate_band's bindings. CLOSED. The factor's bindings were [grant_total, excess_rate], and
  grant_total plays no part in choosing the rate while chargeable_miles, which its tiers actually test,
  belonged to no factor at all. The bindings are now [grant_total, chargeable_miles, excess_rate]: the
  overage the tiers test is the miles driven less the allowance granted less the grace, so both bindings
  are genuinely this factor's evidence, and every binding disjointness and fork count still holds.

D-8 — the fall-through colliding with a tier on one rate class. CLOSED. heavy_overage_rate_usd was 0.22,
  which is exactly Corporate Negotiated Drive Rate's own excess rate, so on that class two tiers of the
  ladder selected the same value. It is now 0.20, and the light tier's 0.26 is likewise no class's own
  rate (the six classes carry 0.32, 0.29, 0.25, 0.22 and 0.00), so no rate class collapses two tiers into
  one outcome. On this world the overage falls in the light band, so the change does not by itself move the
  scored value; the settlement moves for the reasons under T1-1.

T1-3 / D-9 — who performs the return. ACCEPTED, with the reasoning recorded. lifecycle.transitions declares
  picked_up -> returned "by: system" and the blueprint's summary names only cancellation as the renter's own
  act; both are base and frozen. The drive_return event's own meaning — "The renter returns the vehicle and
  the agreement is closed off" — is what the owner=user tool implements, the persona settles the
  authorisation explicitly, and principle H requires at least one problem of every tree to be the customer's
  own write. Reassigning it to the agent would leave this tree with none, so the tool stays owner=user and
  the tension is recorded rather than papered over.

T1-4 / D-10 — the drive_return trigger's mileage line. ACCEPTED, with the reasoning recorded. The trigger
  says a return raises a mileage-use line; on this world two such lines already stand, posted by the
  supplier's counter on 2026-09-11 and on 2026-09-16, the morning the keys went into the box. The line the
  trigger calls for is therefore on the ledger before the agreement is closed off, and having the tool raise
  a third would double-count the miles the renter drove. The tool records the return and settles the excess;
  it does not re-post a movement the counter already recorded.

Summary fields after this task's own writes. Both summary fields satisfy their declared identities on
the seeded world, and the grant carries no money, so charges_total_usd still agrees with the rows when
the settlement is computed. The grant does move the allowance without the holding's cached figure
following it, as every task tool in this framework does. What matters for the reading the audit raised
is that the rule and the records no longer disagree about what the mileage rows mean: they are
movements, the rule adds them, and the single figure by which the rule then departs from the raw sum —
the class's included miles for the day lost to the late collection — is the deviation now declared,
clause by clause, in this policy's overwrite.
user_scenario:
Rosalind Achterberg is forty-six, a ceramicist who has just come off a nine-night guided tour of the Rockies with her husband and their daughter, and she is calling from the kitchen table on her first morning home, tired and talkative and still half in holiday mode. She is friendly, a little scattered, and keeps apologising for not having the paperwork in front of her.

What she wants is simple enough in her own words: she dropped the hire car back at the Boulder office yesterday morning, the desk was still shut so she left the keys in the box, nobody gave her anything to sign, and she wants the hire closed off properly and to know what she owes for the miles before anything lands on her card unannounced. She says outright that she drove a great deal more than she expected to, because the tour kept sending them off on their own between stops.

If she is asked how to find her account she reads out the mobile number the rental confirmations came to, 6302517049. If more is wanted to prove who she is she gives her date of birth, 1979-11-30, and then, if that alone will not do, the last four of the passport on file, 1742. She gives none of that until she is asked for it.

She cannot find the agreement number and says so cheerfully; she can say that she picked the car up at the airport on the ninth, a day later than they had booked it for because the tour ran late into Denver, that it was a big estate car, that they kept it two days longer than they had meant to, and that they dropped it in Boulder rather than back at the airport because the tour ended there. She remembers a man at a branch counter writing the mileage down somewhere in the middle of the week when they called in about the ski rack, and she mentions that only if the agent asks whether anybody looked at the car during the hire. She has no idea what the odometer said at the end and says the supplier will have it. If the agent reads her a running total for the hire she says that it sounds about right but that she has not been watching the card closely.

Her Wanderlane membership comes up only if she is asked about it, and then she says she is on the platinum card and has been in the programme for years and hires cars through them fairly often. The guided tour she has just come back from she will mention if the agent asks what the trip was, saying it was a Wanderlane escorted tour, nine nights, booked and paid months ago.

She does not push and she does not suggest what the desk should do. When the agent tells her something has to be put right on the hire before the miles can be settled, she says of course, do what you need to, and waits. When the agent tells her what the miles come to and asks her to close the hire off herself, she says that is less than she had feared, and she does it herself with whatever the agent hands her rather than asking them to do it in her name. Once she hears that the car is recorded as back and the mileage settled, she says thank you, that she can stop worrying about it now, and ends the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.drive_rental_id: The collected Boulder hire, agreement number RA8T61VD4. Basis: the car rental lookup at action 2 returns exactly one rental of the caller's, standing at picked_up, collected at DENA1 on 2026-09-08 and due back at BLDCT, and the tool's schema says the reference is 'the reference number of the car rental agreement the allowance belongs to; read it from the rental record returned by the car rental lookup before this call'. Uniqueness: she holds no other rental, so no second agreement answers the hire she describes.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.miles_granted: 2280. The ledger carries six rental day lines and two extra day lines, so the allowance is granted for the eight days actually charged. The caller holds an Escorted Tour Package standing at travelling that runs nine nights, at or above the long package term, so each of those days carries the touring miles allowance of 220 rather than the class's own 175. The agreement's booked period runs six days, between two and six, so the day total is the per-day miles for every day granted for plus a further half day's miles for the return leg: 8 x 220 + 110 = 1870. An airport surcharge line stands on the ledger and the vehicle was returned to BLDCT rather than the DENA1 branch it was collected from, adding the one-way airport transfer miles of 90. One ski rack line stands and no snow chains line, so the part touring miles of 140 are added. Two additional driver lines stand and the allowance is granted for eight days, adding the multi driver touring miles of 180. 1870 + 90 + 140 + 180 = 2280 whole miles. Any agent reading the same rows converges on it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the renter's own tool for confirming the vehicle is back and settling the miles, and hand it to the caller.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Handing the vehicle back and settling what the hire owes on her own card is the renter's own act; the unlock changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The caller closes the hire off herself: the rental is recorded as returned and the excess mileage on the agreement is settled.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: drive_ext_return_settlement is the only policy that computes an excess mileage settlement, and its result is this call's excess_mileage_charge_usd; the caller performs the write because the vehicle and the card are hers.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.drive_rental_id: The same collected hire, agreement number RA8T61VD4. Basis: the car rental lookup at action 2 returns it as her only rental standing at picked_up, and the tool's schema says the reference is 'the reference number of the renter's own car rental agreement being closed off; read it from the rental record returned by the car rental lookup before this call'. Uniqueness: she holds no other rental, and only a rental standing at confirmed or picked up may carry an optional item at all.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.excess_mileage_charge_usd: 115.65. The rental's ledger records two mileage movements, -1150 posted 2026-09-11 and -1790 posted 2026-09-16, and each row is the miles that movement took off the allowance, so together they are 2940 miles. The vehicle was collected at 08:22 on 2026-09-09 against a booked collection of 08:00 on 2026-09-08, a whole day late, so the rate class's 175 included miles are taken off for that lost day and the miles driven are 2765 — which is also what the rental's own allowance field shows once the grant is read against it. Against the 2280 miles now granted that leaves an overage of 485. No damage recharge stands on the rental and its rental day lines stand for six days, fewer than the grace day threshold of seven, so 60 miles are carried free, leaving 425 chargeable. Four hundred and twenty-five is below the heavy overage threshold of 500 and at or above the light threshold of 150, so each chargeable mile is charged at 0.26 rather than the class's own 0.29: 110.50. The closing movement was posted on 2026-09-16, two days after the booked return of 2026-09-14, and the overage is at or above the light threshold, so the light overage administration charge of 18.00 is added once to that product, giving 128.50. The caller's active Wanderlane Platinum membership carries two car rental accruals inside the last twenty-four months, at the club driving threshold, so the middle club relief of 10 per cent applies once to the sum: 115.65.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the rental's ledger carries two mileage movements and not one mileage grant, and the holding's own allowance figure stands at -2940 miles, which is exactly those two movements with nothing granted behind them. unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The grant write lands one line of 2280 miles with event type drive_mileage_grant on the rental, so the allowance stands granted and the miles counted beyond it fall from 2765 to 485.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has a single edge and therefore one legal order: the allowance, then the settlement. There are no parallel prerequisites to reorder.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the grant and replaying everything else leaves the overage at 2765 miles and 2705 chargeable after grace, which lifts the rate to the heavy band, so the settlement computes as 518.40 instead of 115.65 — the scored parameter moves by 402.75.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never mentions an included allowance, a mileage grant or anything missing from the hire. Rosalind says only that the car is back, that she drove further than she meant to, and that she wants to know what the miles cost; she never asks whether something must be put right first. Her only contribution to the prerequisite is the passive branch in which, after the agent has explained that something has to be put right on the hire, she says to do what is needed — without asking what it is.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: close_rental_return_9b1c513c in task_tools.py reads the rental row only to copy the customer reference onto the new line, then creates the excess mileage line and updates the rental's status and return stamp; it never looks for a mileage grant, never errors and never hints. grant_included_mileage_444a2a24 likewise creates its line unconditionally. Settling the miles first would succeed and simply write a wrong figure.
